# How to read this cookbook {#sec-how-to-read .unnumbered}

This cookbook provides solutions to a range of problems. It is illustrative and educational and is not the reference manual. Each recipe explicates one feature in the same way, borrowed from @Beazley2013:

- **Problem**: what you are trying to do.
- **Solution**: the self-contained code that does it.
- **Discussion**: why it works, and what to watch for.
- **The check**: validation; the thing the pytest suite asserts; collapsed by default. A broken invariant fails this render.

The recipes here are all attached to an example in DecL, in a library entry's `doc{{{…}}}` in `src/aggregate/agg/library.agg`. Those pages are generated by `aggregate.cookbook`. The same text is executed by `tests/test_library_recipes.py`, so the page you are reading and the test that guards it cannot drift apart, because they share the same source. Fetch one directly with `build.recipe('LimitProfile')`, or survey them with `build.recipes`.

The pricing background (distortions, bounds, allocation) follows
@Mildenhall2022a; the FFT compound-distribution engine follows @Mildenhall2024, which in turn was based on @Grubel1999.
